title: Flutter Rules
summary: Project rules for Flutter apps: feature folders, one state solution, const widgets, ThemeData tokens and widget and unit tests.
description: These rules give a Flutter project a predictable layout and a single way to manage state, so an agent adds features without inventing a new pattern each time.
They focus on practices that keep frames smooth and code reviewable: const constructors, small widgets, centralized theming and tests that pump real widgets.
useWhen: You start a new Flutter app
State is handled with a mix of setState and several packages
Colors and text styles are hard-coded across screens
body:
# Project rules: Flutter

## Layout
- Organize by feature: `lib/features/<name>/{data,domain,presentation}`, with shared code in `lib/core`. Keep `main.dart` to bootstrapping.
- Enable `flutter_lints` or stricter in `analysis_options.yaml` and fix every warning.

## State
- Choose one solution per app (Riverpod or Bloc) and use it everywhere. Keep `setState` for purely local, ephemeral UI state.
- State classes are immutable. Widgets read state and call methods; they do not call repositories or HTTP directly.

## Widgets
- Prefer small widget classes over helper methods returning widgets. Mark constructors and literals `const`.
- Use `ListView.builder` for long lists, give items keys when order changes, and dispose controllers, focus nodes and subscriptions.
- Never use `BuildContext` after an `await` without checking `mounted`.

## Theming and text
- Define colors, typography and spacing in `ThemeData` and extensions; read them via `Theme.of(context)`. Put user-facing strings in localization files.

## Quality
- Write unit tests for logic and widget tests with `pumpWidget` for screens. Use golden tests sparingly.
- Run `dart format --set-exit-if-changed .`, `flutter analyze` and `flutter test` before finishing.

example.prompt: Add a favorites tab that persists across launches
example.result: The agent adds a favorites feature folder, a Riverpod notifier with local storage, const widgets using theme tokens and a widget test for toggling.

faq.question: Why only one state package?
faq.answer: Mixed approaches make every feature a new reading exercise and invite sync bugs between them.

faq.question: Are golden tests required?
faq.answer: No. They are allowed for stable, visual components but are not a default.

access: Instructions only; it does not read or run anything by itself
